ei.title: Chapter 3-09: When a Star Performer Becomes a Boss
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice reflecting on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. If you were a star, be aware that the very success that produced your promotion can now work against you.

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management ①<u>particularly</u> difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to ②<u>give up</u> the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much ③<u>coaching</u> themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice ④<u>to reflect</u> on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. If you were a star, be aware that the very success that produced your promotion can now work against you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: practice + V-ing 구문에서 동명사 reflecting이 필요. to부정사 to reflect는 practice 뒤에 불가.
det.analysis:
① <u>particularly</u> — 부사, particularly difficult 정상

② <u>give up</u> — 구동사, reluctant to give up 정상

③ <u>coaching</u> — 동명사, needed much coaching 정상

④ <u>to reflect</u> — 원문 reflecting. practice + V-ing 구문에서 to부정사 불가. had little practice reflecting (O) / to reflect (X) ←정답
det.tip: practice + V-ing: practice reflecting (O) / practice to reflect (X). practice는 동명사를 목적어로 취함

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before ①<u>becoming</u> a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think ②<u>producing</u> their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to ③<u>deal</u> with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice reflecting on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. If you were a star, be ④<u>aware</u> that the very success that produced your promotion can now work against you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 관계대명사절 동사 자리에 produced(과거시제)가 필요. producing(분사)은 주절 동사 불가.
det.analysis:
① <u>becoming</u> — 동명사, before becoming a manager 정상

② <u>producing</u> — 원문 produced. 'practices they think produced their success'에서 관계사절 동사 자리에 분사 불가 ←정답

③ <u>deal</u> — 원형, how to deal with 정상

④ <u>aware</u> — 형용사 보어, be aware that 정상
det.tip: 관계사절 동사: produced (과거시제, O) / producing (분사, X)

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices ①<u>they thinking</u> produced their success thus far, and they're ②<u>unwilling</u> to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never ③<u>failed</u>, they've had little practice reflecting on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. If you were a star, be aware that the very success that produced your ④<u>promotion</u> can now work against you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 삽입절 'they think'에서 주어+동사 구조 필수. 'they thinking'은 동사 없이 분사만 사용하여 비문.
det.analysis:
① <u>they thinking</u> — 원문 they think. 삽입절에서 주어(they) 뒤에 동사(think) 필요. thinking만으로는 절을 구성 불가 ←정답

② <u>unwilling</u> — 형용사, they're unwilling 정상

③ <u>failed</u> — 과거분사, they've never failed 정상

④ <u>promotion</u> — 명사, produced your promotion 정상
det.tip: 삽입절: they think (S+V, O) / they thinking (V 없음, X)

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly ①<u>difficult</u>. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably ②<u>reluctant</u> to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to ③<u>neglect</u> or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들을 '성장시키다(develop)'는 맥락에서 '무시하다(neglect)'는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>difficult</u> (어려운) — 관리직 전환이 어렵다, 적절

② <u>reluctant</u> (꺼리는) — 변화를 꺼린다, 적절

③ <u>neglect</u> (무시하다) — 원문 develop(성장시키다). 사람을 성장시키고 코칭한다는 맥락에서 neglect 부적절 ←정답

④ <u>mediocre</u> (평범한) — 평범한 상사가 된다, 적절
det.tip: develop(성장시키다) ↔ neglect(무시하다, 방치하다)

Because of their previous ①<u>success</u>, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're ②<u>willing</u> to change themselves. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 자신을 바꾸는 것을 '꺼리는(unwilling)'인데 'willing(기꺼이 하는)'은 반대.
det.analysis:
① <u>success</u> (성공) — 이전의 성공, 적절

② <u>willing</u> (기꺼이 하는) — 원문 unwilling(꺼리는). 변화를 꺼린다는 맥락에서 willing 부적절 ←정답

③ <u>motivation</u> (동기) — 동기 부족, 적절

④ <u>against</u> — 불리하게 작용(work against), 적절
det.tip: unwilling(꺼리는) ↔ willing(기꺼이 하는)

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the __________ they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice reflecting on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 성공을 만들어냈다고 생각하는 '태도와 관행'을 포기하기 꺼린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① attitudes and practices (태도와 관행) — 이전 성공을 만든 것으로 여기는 태도와 관행을 포기하기 꺼린다는 맥락 ←정답

❌ ② failures and setbacks (실패와 좌절) — 실패 경험이 없다는 맥락과 모순

❌ ③ coaching and mentoring (코칭과 멘토링) — 코칭을 받지 않았다는 맥락이지 포기 대상이 아님

❌ ④ promotions and rewards (승진과 보상) — 승진은 결과이지 포기 대상이 아님
det.tip: attitudes and practices = 태도와 관행. 성공의 원인으로 여기는 것

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice __________ experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경험을 '성찰하고 배우는' 연습이 부족했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reflecting on and learning from (성찰하고 배우는) — 실패 경험이 없어 성찰과 학습 연습이 부족하다는 맥락 ←정답

❌ ② ignoring and moving past (무시하고 넘기는) — 성찰의 반대. 연습이 부족하다는 것은 하고 싶어도 못한 것

❌ ③ creating and documenting (만들고 기록하는) — 맥락 부적합

❌ ④ enjoying and celebrating (즐기고 축하하는) — 맥락 부적합
det.tip: reflecting on and learning from experience = 경험을 성찰하고 배우는 것

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change themselves. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 이전 성공이 변화를 꺼리게 만드는 요인 — reluctant to give up.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 코칭 향상 (관리자가 되면 코칭 능력이 향상) — 반대. 코칭하는 법을 모름

❌ ② 실패→성찰 (실패 경험으로 성찰) — 반대. never failed

✅ ③ 성공이 변화 방해 (이전 성공이 변화를 방해) — reluctant to give up + work against ←정답

❌ ④ 뛰어난 관리자 (대부분 뛰어남) — 반대. mediocre bosses
det.tip: 이전 성공 = 변화 방해 요인

ch: 스타 직원들은 관리자가 되면 코칭 능력이 향상된다.
스타 직원들은 실패 경험을 통해 성찰 능력을 키웠다.
이전의 성공은 관리자로서의 변화를 방해하는 요인이 된다.
대부분의 이전 스타들은 뛰어난 관리자로 성장한다.

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 관리자가 된 후 더 높은 성과 — 반대. mediocre bosses.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 동기 부족한 사람 — 문장4 일치

❌ ② 코칭 부재 — 문장3 일치

❌ ③ 실패 부족→성찰 부정적 — 문장5 일치

✅ ④ 더 높은 성과 (관리자 후 더 높은 성과) — 반대. mediocre bosses ←정답
det.tip: mediocre = 평범한 ≠ 더 높은 성과

ch: 스타 직원들은 동기 부족한 사람들을 다루기 어려워한다.
스타 직원들은 자신이 코칭을 많이 받았다고 생각하지 않는다.
스타 직원들의 실패 경험 부족은 성찰 능력에 부정적 영향을 준다.
스타 직원들은 관리자가 된 후 이전보다 더 높은 성과를 낸다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 성찰 연습이 풍부 — 반대. had little practice.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 높은 성과→전환 어려움 — 문장1 일치

❌ ② 성공 방식 고수 — 문장2 reluctant to give up 일치

✅ ③ 성찰 연습 풍부 (경험에서 배우는 연습이 풍부) — 반대. little practice ←정답

❌ ④ 성공→불리 — 문장7 work against 일치
det.tip: had little practice ≠ 풍부

ch: 관리직 전환이 특히 어려운 이유는 이전의 높은 성과와 관련이 있다.
이전 스타들은 성공 방식을 고수하려는 경향이 있다.
스타 직원들은 경험에서 배우는 연습이 풍부하다.
승진을 가져온 성공이 관리자에게 불리하게 작용할 수 있다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이전 성과자가 관리자가 될 때 직면하는 어려움.
det.analysis:
❌ ① benefits of failure (실패의 이점) — 실패 이점이 아닌 실패 부재의 문제

✅ ② challenges of former high performers (이전 성과자의 관리자 전환 어려움) — 글 전체 주제 ←정답

❌ ③ coaching strategies (코칭 전략) — 전략 제시가 아닌 문제 진단

❌ ④ importance of motivation (동기의 중요성) — 동기는 부분적 주제
det.tip: 주제 = 이전 성과자의 관리자 전환 어려움

ch: The benefits of failure in developing leadership skills

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개인 성과자로서의 이전 성공이 관리자 전환 시 장애가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① past success = obstacle (이전 성공이 관리자 전환의 장애) — 글의 핵심 메시지 ←정답

❌ ② mandatory coaching (필수 코칭 훈련) — 글에 주장 없음

❌ ③ failure most important (실패가 가장 중요) — 과도한 일반화

❌ ④ personal style over team (개인 스타일 우선) — 반대. 이것이 문제
det.tip: 요지 = 이전 성공이 관리자로서의 장애가 될 수 있다

ch: Past success as an individual performer can become an obstacle when transitioning to a management role.

det.korean: 성공이 불리하게 작용 = 관리자로서 오히려 방해가 됨.
det.analysis:

❌ ② 동료 갈등 (동료와 갈등) — 글에 동료 갈등 언급 없음

❌ ③ 업무량 증가 (체력 소모) — 글에 업무량 언급 없음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 They가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문장3의 They = 이전의 스타 직원들 (문장2의 stars).

questions.passage: If you were a high performer in your work before becoming a manager, you may find the journey into management particularly difficult. Because of their previous success, stars are understandably reluctant to give up the attitudes and practices they think produced their success thus far, and they're unwilling to change <u>themselves</u>. They don't know how to develop or coach people because they never needed much coaching themselves, or so they believe. They don't know how to deal with people who lack their motivation. Because they've never failed, they've had little practice reflecting on and learning from experience. No wonder many former stars turn into mediocre bosses. If you were a star, be aware that the very success that produced your promotion can now work against you.
